item.claim: More patients discontinued because of adverse events on drug R (6.0%) than on placebo (2.3%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports that 6.0% of patients on Drug R and 2.3% on placebo discontinued because of a TEAE.

item.claim: At week 26, drug R reduced HbA1c by 0.94% compared with 0.28% on placebo (difference -0.66%, p < 0.001).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports the stated Week 26 changes, difference, and p-value.

item.claim: Body weight decreased by 2.1 kg with drug R and 0.6 kg with placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Body weight, kg, LS mean change (SE) | -2.1 (0.3) | -0.6 (0.3)
result.reason: The table reports week 26 LS mean weight changes of -2.1 kg with Drug R and -0.6 kg with placebo.

item.claim: Nearly 40% of drug R patients reached HbA1c below 7.0% at week 26, versus about 22% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports 39.9% of Drug R patients and 21.8% of placebo patients with HbA1c below 7.0% at week 26.

item.claim: Systolic blood pressure fell numerically more with drug R, but the difference from placebo was not statistically significant (p = 0.247).
item.label: supported

result.reason: Drug R had a numerically greater reduction than placebo, and the reported p-value was 0.247.

item.claim: Nausea was the most common adverse event with drug R, reported by 12.0% of patients versus 4.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: Nausea is the most frequent listed event with Drug R, and the table reports 12.0% with Drug R versus 4.0% with placebo.

item.claim: Hypoglycaemia (glucose below 54 mg/dL) was reported in 4.0% of patients on drug R and 1.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports hypoglycaemia below 54 mg/dL in 4.0% of patients on drug R and 1.0% on placebo.

item.claim: Fasting plasma glucose fell by 24.3 mg/dL on drug R versus 8.9 mg/dL on placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Fasting plasma glucose, mg/dL, LS mean change (SE) | -24.3 (2.1) | -8.9 (2.1)
result.reason: The table reports LS mean changes of −24.3 mg/dL on Drug R and −8.9 mg/dL on placebo at week 26.

item.claim: Shifts in ALT to more than three times the upper limit of normal were rare (0.7% on drug R, 0.3% on placebo).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports shifts to >3x ULN in ALT for 0.7% on Drug R and 0.3% on placebo, matching the claim.

item.claim: The treatment effect on HbA1c was consistent across age subgroups (interaction p = 0.61).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports an age-subgroup interaction p-value of 0.61, supporting the claim that the treatment effect was consistent across age subgroups.

item.claim: Drug R reduced HbA1c significantly more than placebo at every visit through week 52.
item.label: supported

result.quote:
Week 12 ... p-value <0.001
Week 26 ... p-value <0.001
Week 52 ... p-value <0.001
result.reason: The table shows significantly greater reductions at weeks 12, 26, and 52, but does not establish significance at every visit through week 52 beyond those listed visits.

item.claim: One patient on drug R and two on placebo died during the study.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports one death in the Drug R group and two in the placebo group.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction appeared smaller in patients with eGFR below 60 (difference -0.38%) than in those with eGFR of 60 or above (-0.72%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The reported differences are -0.38% for eGFR below 60 and -0.72% for eGFR of 60 or above, consistent with the claim that the reduction appeared smaller in the lower-eGFR subgroup.

item.claim: Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups; mean age was 61.2 and 60.8 years and mean HbA1c 8.3% and 8.2%.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The reported age and HbA1c means match the claim and are similar between groups, consistent with the characterization of these baseline characteristics as balanced.

item.claim: Drug R did not increase the risk of hypoglycaemia.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Hypoglycaemia was reported more often with Drug R than placebo (4.0% vs 1.0%), so the table does not support the claim that Drug R did not increase its risk.

item.claim: Drug R is safe in patients with renal impairment.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Overview of treatment-emergent adverse events (safety population)
result.reason: The source reports overall safety-population adverse events and does not establish safety specifically in patients with renal impairment.

item.claim: No safety signals were identified for hepatic or renal function.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: eGFR fell 2.9 vs 1.1; 'no signal' is a conclusion the table can't make

result.reason: The table reports ALT elevations and changes in eGFR but does not establish the broader claim that no hepatic or renal safety signals were identified.

item.claim: Gastrointestinal events were mild and transient.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: severity and duration aren't in the table

result.reason: The table reports the frequency of nausea and diarrhoea but does not establish that the events were mild or transient.

item.claim: Drug R was well tolerated, with an adverse event profile similar to placebo.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: drug-related 24.0 vs 13.8, discontinuation 6.0 vs 2.3, grade>=3 9.0 vs 6.0

result.quote:
Drug-related TEAE | 72 (24.0) | 41 (13.8)
Grade 3 or higher TEAE | 27 (9.0) | 18 (6.0)
TEAE leading to discontinuation | 18 (6.0) | 7 (2.3)
result.reason: The table reports higher rates of drug-related, Grade 3 or higher, and discontinuation-leading adverse events with Drug R than with placebo, so it does not establish a similar adverse event profile.

item.claim: Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates in the two groups (7.0% and 6.4%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The source reports serious TEAE rates of 7.0% and 6.4%, which supports the claim that the rates were similar.

item.claim: The HbA1c benefit of drug R was consistent across renal function subgroups.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The interaction p-value is 0.04 and the eGFR <60 subgroup confidence interval includes zero, so the source does not establish a consistent benefit across renal function subgroups.

item.claim: In patients with eGFR below 60, drug R significantly reduced HbA1c versus placebo (difference -0.38%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The reported difference is -0.38%, but its 95% CI includes zero, so the table does not support that the reduction was statistically significant.

item.claim: Older patients (65 years and above) derived a significantly smaller benefit than younger patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The estimated benefit is numerically smaller in patients aged 65 or older, but the age interaction p-value of 0.61 does not support a significantly smaller benefit.

item.claim: At week 52, drug R reduced body weight by 2.1 kg.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.2: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)
result.reason: The source reports the 2.1 kg reduction at week 26, not week 52.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction with drug R increased steadily through week 52.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The reduction became larger through week 26 but was smaller at week 52, so it did not increase steadily through week 52.

item.claim: The maximal HbA1c reduction was reached by week 12.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The largest HbA1c reduction shown is at week 26 (-0.94), not week 12 (-0.72).

item.claim: Drug R also lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: Although the estimated difference favors Drug R, the confidence interval includes zero and p=0.247, so the source does not establish that Drug R lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.

item.claim: In the safety population, HbA1c fell by 0.94% at week 26.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Title: Change from baseline in HbA1c (%) by visit (full analysis set, MMRM)
result.reason: The table reports the 0.94% decrease at week 26 for the full analysis set, not the safety population.

item.claim: Drug R caused urinary tract infections in 5.0% of patients.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: 5.0 vs 4.7 on placebo; incidence isn't causation

result.reason: The table reports urinary tract infections in 5.0% of Drug R patients but does not establish that Drug R caused them.

item.claim: Drug R provides an additional blood pressure benefit of 1.3 mmHg.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The estimated difference is 1.3 mmHg in Drug R’s favor, but the confidence interval includes no difference and p=0.247, so the source does not establish an additional blood pressure benefit.

item.claim: Any adverse event was reported by 57.0% of drug R patients and 61.0% of placebo patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source reports any TEAE in 61.0% of Drug R patients and 57.0% of placebo patients, the reverse of the claim.

item.claim: Weight loss with drug R was driven by its gastrointestinal effects.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports weight changes but does not establish that weight loss was driven by gastrointestinal effects.

item.claim: Headache was more common with drug R than with placebo (3.7% vs 4.4%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The percentages match, but headache was less common with drug R than with placebo, not more common.

item.claim: Drug R tripled the proportion of patients reaching HbA1c below 7.0%.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The proportion was 39.9% with Drug R versus 21.8% with placebo, which is not three times as high.

item.claim: eGFR increased slightly with drug R over 52 weeks.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports that eGFR decreased by 2.9 with Drug R over 52 weeks, rather than increasing.

item.claim: Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 50% more frequent with drug R (9.0% vs 6.0%), all of them drug-related.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: relatedness of grade 3 events not in table

result.reason: The table supports the 9.0% versus 6.0% rates, but does not establish that all Grade 3 or higher events were drug-related.

item.claim: Haematocrit decreased with drug R.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source reports a mean increase in haematocrit with Drug R, not a decrease.
